name: Berlin
tagline: A two-hour line for a döner, and three Michelin stars on Germany's most awarded wine list.

Rutz.description: Avant-garde German cuisine with the country's most awarded wine list. Three Michelin stars.

Zum Schusterjungen.description: Corner Kneipe in Prenzlauer Berg, open for almost a century. Anthony Bourdain ate Eisbein here in the Berlin special of "Parts Unknown."

Curry 36.description: Berlin's benchmark currywurst, with its own merchandise and branded ketchup.

Tim Raue.description: European cuisine with Asian inspiration from chef Tim Raue, among the world's best since opening in 2010. Two Michelin stars, rated 4/5 by Time Out Berlin critic Anna Geary-Meyer.

Markthalle Neun.description: A historic Kreuzberg market turned street food benchmark, famous for its Street Food Thursday.

Nobelhart & Schmutzig.description: Hyper-local fine dining in Kreuzberg: only ingredients from Berlin and Brandenburg, served at a counter with no tablecloths and no written menu. One Michelin star from owner Billy Wagner and chef Micha Schäfer.

Facil.description: Avant-garde cuisine around a bamboo garden hidden on the fifth floor of the Mandala Hotel near Potsdamer Platz. Two Michelin stars held continuously since 2013 under chef Michael Kempf.

Horváth.description: Austrian haute cuisine reinvented by chef Sebastian Frank on the banks of the Landwehr canal in Kreuzberg. Two Michelin stars.

Coda Dessert Dining.description: Germany's only restaurant built entirely around dessert, with no refined sugar, created by pastry chef René Frank. Two Michelin stars in Neukölln.

Restaurant Richard.description: Contemporary French cuisine in a former 1900 ballroom by the Spree, run by painter-turned-chef Hans Richard. One Michelin star since 2015.

Julius.description: The casual sibling of Ernst, the Michelin-starred restaurant that closed at the end of 2024, located right across the street in Wedding with the same chef, Dylan Watson-Brawn.

eins44.description: Market-driven cooking in the third courtyard of a former essence distillery in Neukölln, recommended by the Michelin Guide since 2017.

Bandol sur Mer.description: A tiny, unmarked French bistro on Torstraße, holding one Michelin star since 2016 and a short menu that changes constantly.

Katz Orange.description: Market-driven cooking and slow-cooked meats in the courtyard of a former brick brewery in Mitte, sourced partly from its own farm in Brandenburg.

Zur Letzten Instanz.description: Berlin's oldest restaurant, in continuous operation since 1621 next to the Graues Kloster. Local lore holds that even Napoleon once dined here.

Dicke Wirtin.description: A traditional Kneipe in Charlottenburg near Savignyplatz, serving hearty Berlin dishes for decades alongside a wide selection of draught beers.

Konnopke's Imbiss.description: Berlin's most famous currywurst stand, under the U2 viaduct in Prenzlauer Berg since 1930. It served East Berlin's first currywurst starting in 1960.

Mustafa's Gemüse Kebap.description: Berlin's longest-queued vegetable kebab, served from a small kiosk on Mehringdamm that has gone viral on social media worldwide.

Hasir.description: The original Hasir location on Adalbertstraße, where in 1971 Mehmet Aygün had the idea of putting döner kebab inside flatbread, shaping the döner sandwich as it is known today.

Rüyam Gemüse Kebap.description: Mustafa's great rival in Berlin's endless debate over the best vegetable döner, drawing its own long queues in Schöneberg.

Bonanza Coffee Heroes.description: A pioneer of Berlin's third-wave coffee scene since 2006, roasting on site at its original Prenzlauer Berg location.

The Barn Roastery.description: One of Germany's most influential specialty coffee roasters, with on-site roasting visible at its café on Schönhauser Allee.

Zeit für Brot.description: A Mitte bakery famous for its cinnamon rolls (Zimtschnecken), baked in full view behind a glass window.

Prater Garten.description: Berlin's oldest beer garden, set in a Prenzlauer Berg courtyard since 1837, under century-old chestnut trees with seating for 600.

Golgatha.description: A beer garden atop Kreuzberg's Viktoriapark, next to the artificial waterfall with views over the city.

Café am Neuen See.description: A lakeside beer garden in the heart of Tiergarten, seating several hundred people under chestnut trees.

Borchardt.description: A Berlin institution since 1853 on Gendarmenmarkt, famous for its Wiener Schnitzel and its regular clientele of politicians and actors.

Grill Royal.description: A steakhouse on the banks of the Spree in Mitte, the go-to restaurant for international celebrities since it opened in 2007.

Renger-Patzsch.description: A regional, seasonal-cooking bistro in Schöneberg with a gallery-like atmosphere and a menu that changes daily.

Max und Moritz.description: A historic Kreuzberg brewery-restaurant opened in 1902, named after Wilhelm Busch's comic characters and serving traditional Berlin cuisine.

Cocolo Ramen.description: One of Berlin's first serious ramen-ya, in a small Mitte dining room with broth simmered for hours.

Zwölf Apostel.description: A pizzeria under the S-Bahn arches near Friedrichstraße, famous for its meter-long pizzas.

Fine Bagels.description: New York-style bagels that started in 2013 as an offshoot of the Shakespeare and Sons bookstore, now a destination in its own right in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg.

Princess Cheesecake.description: A tea room and bakery-café in Mitte specializing in cheesecake, open since 2011 next to Monbijoupark.

Defne.description: A Turkish restaurant with a terrace over the Landwehr canal in Kreuzberg, serving mezze and grilled fish beyond the usual döner.

Austria.description: An Austrian restaurant next to Kreuzberg's Marheineke Markthalle, famous for a Wiener Schnitzel that overflows the plate.

Ottenthal.description: An Austrian restaurant and wine shop in Charlottenburg, with a Wiener Schnitzel considered among the city's best.

Witty's.description: Germany's first organic currywurst kiosk, facing the KaDeWe department store since 1984 and Bioland-certified since 2003.

Türkenmarkt am Maybachufer.description: A Turkish market along the Landwehr canal, held every Tuesday and Friday, with cheap produce, freshly baked bread, and takeaway food stalls.

Schneeweiss.description: Alpine cuisine blending Austria, Bavaria, and northern Italy, served in an all-white interior in Friedrichshain.
